sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Chandan’s diagnostics business has a scoreable growth record after separating the pharmacy subsidiary it sold to a group company. Constant-parent sales rose from ₹75.83 crore in FY23 to ₹156.65 crore in FY26, a 27.36% CAGR. Latest parent cash conversion improved, but ₹41.57 crore capex, ₹26.49 crore related-party loans and conditional warrant funding complicate per-share value. BQS 5.34 and GQS 6.5 are supported estimates; IAS remains NS. This is a completed conditional review, not a recommendation to buy.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: NSE Emerge CHANDAN, INE0B2N01016. September 30 actual allotment gives 25,702,062 shares; supersedes historical 24,452,064 and September 14 post-allotment 25,052,062 counts. Remaining 3,200,002 warrants at ₹234; fully diluted 28,902,064 only on exercise. Official master can lag allotments; do not use its stale capital as denominator. Reporting uses Accounting Standards (AS), not Ind AS. The audit report explicitly states that the SME exemption was used and Ind AS was not adopted; the exchange endpoint name does not determine the accounting basis. The dated official close is ₹228.50 on 19 October 2026; review cutoff 20 October. The forecast is explicitly parent-only after pharmacy disposal, not a stitched consolidated growth series. All gates are Conditional. Actual allotments override stale capital fields, and no unreviewed acquisition earnings are added.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 7, CAP 5, CASH 4, BAL 5, EXEC 6 and EARN 5 are supported with company-specific facts and counterevidence. R remains NS; D 4, P 4 and L 7 are separately supported. Exact canonical weights, coverage and bounds are retained without reweighting. There is no persistent low-cash cap: recent parent CFO improved meaningfully, although free cash remains negative after expansion. A valuation-data gap does not erase usable business-quality evidence.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Chandan provides pathology, radiology and diagnostic services through owned centres, laboratories, franchises, private-hospital relationships and government PPP contracts. FY26 disclosures described 313 centres/labs across 16 states, 16 NABL laboratories and 10 PPP radiology contracts. These counts have different economics and cannot be summed as equivalent productive capacity. The provisional September update reported 685 franchises plus 25 comprehensive centres, 19 diagnostic centres, 25 labs and 16 radiology labs. Pharmacy historically added substantial low-margin revenue; its sale changes the forward perimeter rather than destroying the comparable parent diagnostics history.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Regional referral relationships, diagnostic accreditation, local density and PPP access create useful operating advantages. Franchise expansion may improve reach with less direct capital, but does not establish patient throughput or margins. Dr Lal Path Labs’ primary FY26 group statements show ₹2,762.91 crore revenue, ₹509.75 crore PAT, ₹635.61 crore CFO and ₹173.38 crore cash PPE/intangible capex. This is an economic comparison, not a valuation shortcut: Dr Lal is larger, more pathology-focused and uses Ind AS lease accounting, whereas Chandan’s radiology equipment and PPP mix require more capital and different cash-cycle assumptions.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: The audited constant-parent series is ₹75.8334/₹99.8748/₹129.1642/₹156.6473 crore for FY23–26. Three-year CAGR 27.36% supports REV 8 under the short-history cap. Parent PAT rose from ₹4.0416 crore in FY23 to ₹16.0164/₹20.7780/₹25.3413 crore thereafter. Consolidated FY22–26 history includes the pharmacy business and is retained only as a separate diagnostic, not the post-disposal forecast baseline. Provisional Q2 FY27 diagnostic revenue ₹56.3788 crore grew 46.66%; this is unaudited and may include newly acquired units. It does not prove all growth organic.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: March remaining IPO project allocation was ₹16.5457 crore, largely Jankipuram, while warrant-funded expansion/acquisition objects totalled ₹94.5 crore before prior deployment. The model uses ₹98.8703 crore remaining project spending from March across FY27–28, not the full original projects plus already-spent CWIP. Nishkam Imaging and Ansh Diagnostics units were acquired in April and September; prices and target financials were not provided in the inspected disclosures, so no invented profit contribution is credited. October’s equipment-specific ₹5.22 crore sanction funds 90% of a ₹5.8 crore CT scanner at 8.75%, with a 60-month tenor and cash-margin requirement. This is not unrestricted working-capital capacity. The 30 September AGM approved variation of the warrant-use objects, as confirmed by the 2 October voting and scrutinizer report. Approval changes permitted allocation, not evidence of actual deployment or additional cash.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The company disclosed a 31 July 2026 communication withdrawing Dayal Institute of Medical Sciences Limited’s complaint after reconciliation and settlement between the parties; the complainant requested closure by the relevant authorities. Separately, SEBI’s 6 August 2026 administrative warning, attached to the 10 August exchange filing, identified inadequate RHP disclosure concerning partly paid shares held by that institute. The issuer stated that no monetary penalty or restriction was imposed. Withdrawal of the complaint does not erase the later warning, and neither document is described here as a criminal conviction or proof of broader misconduct. Separately, March parent loans to Hospital, Pharmacy and Foundation totalled ₹26.4937 crore, and group guarantees ₹14.5143 crore. Pharmacy equity was sold to Hospital for ₹16.7711 crore for the issuer’s 53.56% stake, not the ₹31.3136 crore whole-company valuation shown elsewhere in the statement. An independent valuation report is cited but was not retrieved; management’s arm’s-length assertion is not independently certified. Amar Singh’s disclosed salary ₹0.4671 crore is separate from ₹1.2859 crore reimbursements. Vinod Jain’s resignation cites other professional commitments and no other material reasons, not an auditor dispute.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Parent FY25 CFO was re-presented from− ₹18.6886 crore to ₹6.3794 crore; CFI moved from− ₹35.7975 crore to− ₹60.8648 crore and CFF by− ₹0.0007 crore, leaving net cash change ₹5.4996 crore unchanged. The consolidated bridge also preserves net cash. This is not missing cash. FY26 parent CFO ₹24.1642 crore less ₹41.5705 crore cash capex leaves− ₹17.4063 crore FCF. Core EBITDA after the unidentified ₹2.7097 crore exceptional charge is ₹43.7215 crore; the charge is not automatically added back. Cash ₹3.1356 crore,FDs ₹13.8602 crore and related-party loans ₹26.4937 crore are distinct. Monitored warrant reserves and unused IPO object budgets are not separate additive free-cash pots. Gross warrant receipts ₹26.0325 crore versus annual net financing ₹21.3346 crore require a ₹4.6979 crore expense/classification bridge; the model uses actual cash, not an invented balancing asset. The Q2 ₹12.03 crore pharmacy-disposal gain is nonrecurring and not diagnostic operating profit. The 29 May 2026 audit opinion on the standalone annual results is unmodified. That opinion does not independently resolve subsequent receipt, deposit-restriction or related-party recoverability questions.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Current 25,702,062 shares at ₹228.50 imply ₹587.29 crore market value, about 23.18× FY26 parent PAT before valuing surviving subsidiaries separately. The funded parent-only model has bear/base/bull growth 8%/18%/26%, core margins 23%/28%/31%, NWC 40%/32%/27% and exit EV/EBITDA 8/12/16. Annual models include expansion and maintenance, working capital, scheduled repayments, half-year interest on new draws, disposal tax, earmarked cash and warrant dilution. Bear assumes no further exercise; base/bull receive ₹56.1600 crore with 3,200,002 new shares in FY28. Conditional bear/base/bull terminal prices ₹156.47/₹459.33/₹923.63 imply annual returns -7.29%/14.99%/32.23%. R stays NS because receipt/deployment, acquisition costs and group asset recovery remain unresolved. No recurring pharmacy gain or cash-free dilution is used. Tax on the recognized disposal gain is retained even if sale cash is delayed; after the CT loan’s first modeled year, a blended scenario borrowing rate applies to all debt. Opening income tax payable of ₹3.6125 crore is now explicitly removed from the operating-WC credit and settled once in FY27. That tax-only reclassification has no economic effect; the additional employee/deposit claims below do change the funded returns. The ₹0.539 crore long-term tax refund is not credited because recovery timing is unverified. The opening-claim bridge also pays ₹0.962200 crore of excluded current employee/interest claims once in FY27, and retains ₹4.160600 crore of net noncurrent employee/deposit claims as a terminal equity deduction. It does not force noncurrent claims into immediate repayment. Future operating compensation is cash funded with the opening net deficit held constant; existing taxes, capital creditors and normal WC liabilities are not charged twice.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: PPP/private-hospital collection delays can coincide with equipment spending and warrant non-exercise. Related loans and guarantees can transmit group stress into the listed issuer, even after pharmacy equity is sold. The severe model combines declining revenue, 16% margin, 50% NWC, 15% borrowing cost, no remaining warrant exercise, no pharmacy cash receipt, unavailable earmarked FD, ₹20 crore extra project cost and all ₹14.5143 crore guarantees called. These are stresses, not predictions or findings of default. Ordinary disclosed consumer/labour/tax cases remain attributed contingencies; they are not all criminal proceedings. Separate sensitivities distinguish loan recovery, guarantee calls, equipment funding and dilution rather than hiding them inside one terminal multiple. With all identified opening claims included, severe peak required debt is ₹206.5797 crore and terminal price is ₹0.0000; these are conditional requirements, not committed facilities.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold/tenfold current market values are about ₹2,936 crore/₹5,873 crore before future dilution. At an illustrative 25× P/E and 16% net margin they need ₹734 crore/₹1,468 crore diagnostics sales, about 4.7×/9.4× the parent baseline, before debt/cash or surviving-subsidiary adjustments. Full remaining warrant exercise increases shares by 12.45%, raising the operating hurdle for equivalent per-share gains. Network-count targets alone do not prove patient volume, equipment utilisation or cash-funded returns. The bull model is a conditional route, not confirmation of a multibagger outcome.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Reconcile actual bank receipts, issue costs and restrictions against both IPO and warrant utilisation schedules; never equate object balances with free cash. Obtain post-disposal pharmacy loan/guarantee status and the underlying valuation report. Confirm acquisition consideration and commissioning/capacity utilization at newly acquired and greenfield sites. Separate recurring diagnostic income from disposal gains and related-interest income. Track cash collection and actual scheduled debt service. Warrant exercise must be monitored with both cash and shares, especially while the dated share price is below ₹234. The 60-observed-session turnover implies 1.30 exit days for ₹5 lakh at 5% participation, but ₹182,800 lots and exchange concentration flags require live depth checks.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed deep conditional hold. Parent growth and improving operating cash are genuine strengths, while external group exposure, disclosure history and expansion funding limit conviction. All supported quality factors remain scored; IAS is NS because material expected-return inputs are unresolved, not because annual funding work is absent. Reconsider after bank/proceeds reconciliation, capital deployment evidence, related-party recovery/guarantee clarification and per-share execution are verified.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The review uses audited FY24 standalone scans, FY25/FY26 annual reports, final prospectus, June revised results, actual September allotments, two CRISIL monitoring reports, pharmacy disposal statement, Q2 provisional update, acquisition/sanction filings and original SEBI warning plus settlement withdrawal. The source ledger distinguishes primary disclosures from management claims. The linked annual model links five annual operating/funding rows and terminal equity for every case; source assumptions do not replace missing actual cash or acquisition prices. Opening claims are reconciled separately: current exclusions settle once, normal operating balances remain in WC, and net noncurrent employee/deposit claims reduce terminal equity without an unsupported immediate-payout assumption.

limitations: This is a March balance-sheet model with explicitly timed subsequent events, not an asserted October net-debt measurement. Actual interim operating cash and project payments are not invented.

FY26 annual net financing inflow from warrants is 21.3346, versus monitor gross receipts of 26.0325, a difference of 4.6979. Net expenses or classification may explain it, but a detailed bridge is unavailable. No missing-cash inference is made; actual March cash is never inflated by this difference.

Unused IPO and warrant object budgets are not additive bank balances. Only the monitored March warrant bank/deposit reserve of 9.1017119 is credited. Other deposits of 6.5495189 and unverified IPO cash are not assumed freely available.

Pharmacy equity-sale recognition appears in the Q2 provisional update. Cash receipt timing and release of related guarantees and loans are unconfirmed. Receipt delay, unavailable deposits, loan recovery and guarantee-call sensitivities test the consequences.
Pending warrants may expire without exercise, particularly if the market remains below ₹234. Full exercise is conditional and links cash to new shares; separate scenarios assume no exercise.

Post-March Nishkam and Ansh asset-unit acquisition prices and asset allocations are unavailable. The main project budget includes expansion. Additional ₹10 crore and ₹20 crore cases test unprovided costs rather than inventing target profits.
The October CT loan is equipment-specific, not general working-capital headroom. Other new borrowing is a modelled requirement, not a committed facility.
Related-party loans of 26.4937, guarantees of 14.5143 and the unreviewed pharmacy valuation report remain capital-allocation limitations. Their existence alone does not imply wrongdoing.

Parent-only terminal value excludes surviving diagnostic-subsidiary profits and book investments rather than inventing a consolidated minority bridge. Apparent upside and downside are conditional scenarios, not a precise fair value.

opening.NWC_formula: Inventory 16.2318 + receivables 44.215 + other current assets 7.3846 − payables 10.0665 − operating current liabilities 4.7374 (8.3499 total less 3.6125 income tax payable). Related-party loans 26.4937 and financial deposits are excluded. Existing operating security deposits 3.2932 remain in this conservative NWC base.

valuation.formulas: Parent-only revenue excludes pharmacy and does not add unsupported subsidiary earnings. Core margin begins near reported EBITDA after the exceptional charge; the unidentified charge is not automatically added back. Sales compound annually. Operating tax is 26% of positive EBIT less solved interest. Operating CFO deducts the change in NWC. Opening income tax payable of 3.6125 is removed from the opening NWC credit and paid separately once in FY27; the equal and opposite opening bridge leaves cash and return outputs unchanged. The 0.539 long-term tax refund is excluded from free cash and terminal value because recovery timing is unverified. FCF funds project and maintenance capex, the new CT cash-margin deposit of 0.58, disposal tax and guarantee-call sensitivities. Remaining March IPO project spending of 16.5457 plus warrant-funded project spending of 82.3246119 totals 98.8703119 across FY27–28; costs already incurred in CWIP are excluded from new spending. Only the verified March warrant reserve of 9.1017119 is credited, not an additional 16.5457 of IPO object budgets as cash. Actual September conversion cash of 21.9374649 enters FY27 once; the June increment is not added again. The pharmacy sale of 16.771055424 is a conditional cash receipt earmarked for projects, not recurring profit. Tax on the recognized gain is paid in FY27 even when collection is delayed. Pending-warrant 75% cash of 56.1600351 enters FY28 with 3,200,002 new shares only if exercised. The CT sanction of 5.22 is drawn in FY27 against included project spending, not treated as current debt. Its first-year interest uses half a year at 8.75%; thereafter the scenario blended rate applies to all outstanding debt, an explicit rate/refinancing simplification. Existing scheduled debt repayments are 10.0311 in FY27 and 7.25 thereafter at year-end, with any refinancing gap explicitly borrowed. Ordinary surplus repayments occur at year-end. New draws incur half-year interest, solved jointly with tax. The cash floor is 2. Terminal equity is the greater of zero and core EBITDA times exit multiple, less debt plus free cash. No additional value is credited for excluded deposits, related loans, subsidiaries or restricted reserves; recovery tests are separate. Annual return equals (terminal price / 228.5) raised to 0.2, less one. Opening-claim extension: first-year CFO includes the separately settled opening tax and excluded current employee/interest claims. Previously accrued taxes and capital creditors are not paid twice. Old unpaid dividends are financing cash outflows without new buyer entitlement. Net noncurrent employee/deposit claims reduce terminal equity once, while normal WC liabilities remain within the operating cash bridge.
valuation.interest_timing_convention: New borrowing incurs half-year interest in the year drawn. Ordinary excess-cash repayments occur at year-end and receive no same-year interest saving. Curis collateral-funded FD overdraft repayment retains its explicit half-year timing. Interest, positive-profit cash tax and funding draw are solved jointly to a 1e-12 crore tolerance; new borrowing is a funding requirement, not a committed facility.
limitations: This is a March balance-sheet model with explicitly timed subsequent events, not an asserted October net-debt measurement. Actual interim operating cash and project payments are not invented.

FY26 annual net financing inflow from warrants is 21.3346, versus monitor gross receipts of 26.0325, a difference of 4.6979. Net expenses or classification may explain it, but a detailed bridge is unavailable. No missing-cash inference is made; actual March cash is never inflated by this difference.

Unused IPO and warrant object budgets are not additive bank balances. Only the monitored March warrant bank/deposit reserve of 9.1017119 is credited. Other deposits of 6.5495189 and unverified IPO cash are not assumed freely available.

Pharmacy equity-sale recognition appears in the Q2 provisional update. Cash receipt timing and release of related guarantees and loans are unconfirmed. Receipt delay, unavailable deposits, loan recovery and guarantee-call sensitivities test the consequences.
Pending warrants may expire without exercise, particularly if the market remains below ₹234. Full exercise is conditional and links cash to new shares; separate scenarios assume no exercise.

Post-March Nishkam and Ansh asset-unit acquisition prices and asset allocations are unavailable. The main project budget includes expansion. Additional ₹10 crore and ₹20 crore cases test unprovided costs rather than inventing target profits.
The October CT loan is equipment-specific, not general working-capital headroom. Other new borrowing is a modelled requirement, not a committed facility.
Related-party loans of 26.4937, guarantees of 14.5143 and the unreviewed pharmacy valuation report remain capital-allocation limitations. Their existence alone does not imply wrongdoing.

Parent-only terminal value excludes surviving diagnostic-subsidiary profits and book investments rather than inventing a consolidated minority bridge. Apparent upside and downside are conditional scenarios, not a precise fair value.
